subject: Model fit evals: tool-calling & structured output follow-up
summary: Post-discovery follow-up with Avery Analytics: share prompt sets, recommended models, benchmark links; align on structured-output evals and retry strategy for tool-calling JSON schema compliance.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@averyanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up + prompt sets & next steps (Avery Analytics)

Hi Taylor —

Thanks again for the conversation today — great overview of the use cases and the runbook you have for structured customer responses. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Attached: a first draft prompt set (avery_prompt_set_v1.json) and a small sample benchmark run we used internally (benchmark_run_20270410.csv).
- Recommended next steps: 1) You share a ~1000-row sample of anonymized production prompts and expected JSON schema; 2) We run a short model-fit eval (tool-calling + structured-output) and share a results dashboard; 3) Sync next Tuesday to review results and iterate on schema/validation rules.

On the model front, initial recommendations are included below — we'll validate with the sample dataset:
- redwood-stream-2-8b: best latency/cost balance for interactive flows
- redwood-opt-1-16b-quant: higher-quality option if you need stricter schema adherence and fewer retries

Two quick notes on structured output & tool-calling: we pay special attention to JSON schema compliance (presence/type/extra fields) and run retry/backoff logic at the client/runtime layer when outputs are invalid. We'll include baseline pass/fail rates and a suggested retry policy in the eval report.

If that plan sounds good, please reply with the sample and your canonical JSON schema and I'll kick off the eval.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: avery_prompt_set_v1.json (text), benchmark_run_20270410.csv (csv)

From: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@averyanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T18:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + prompt sets & next steps (Avery Analytics)

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap and quick turnaround. Plan sounds good. A couple of quick clarifications before we send the sample: 

- JSON schema: we have a canonical schema for our customer-facing payloads; I'll attach it and a 500-row anonymized sample by EOD Monday.
- Retries: what's the default behavior you recommend for tool-calling failures when the model returns malformed JSON? We're worried about downstream systems choking if retries keep producing invalid payloads.

On cost/latency: our SLA target is 350ms p95 for the interactive flow, but we can accept slightly higher latency if schema compliance improves.

Thanks,
Taylor
Product Lead | Avery Analytics
taylor@averyanalytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@averyanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + prompt sets & next steps (Avery Analytics)

Taylor —

Thanks — that timeline works. Leaving you the high-level answers and artifacts we usually share for structured-output evals: 

1) Recommended models (to evaluate in parallel):
   - redwood-stream-2-8b — low-latency baseline; good at following instructions with prompt engineering
   - redwood-opt-1-16b-quantized — higher fidelity on schema constraints, especially when combined with structured-output constraints (few-shot examples + schema annotations)
   - redwood-llm-7b-retrieval — if you need retrieval-augmented contexts for long customer histories (optional)

2) Typical eval checklist we'll run:
   - Schema pass/fail (strict JSON parse)
   - Field-level type checks and value normalization (dates, enums)
   - Extra-field detection and mitigation (we add strict post-parsing filters)
   - Retry behaviour: default is up to 2 automatic retries with prompt augmentation (explicit "Fix JSON" instructions + a concise example). If still invalid, mark as failure and route to a safe fallback (empty object or human-in-loop depending on severity).

3) Deliverables: detailed CSV with per-example model output, flags for parse/validation failures, a summary dashboard, and suggested prompt/template tweaks.

4) Links and attachments: benchmark run (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/benchmark-avery-2027) and prompt set (attached).

If you can send the schema and sample, we'll start the run and aim to have preliminary results within 48 hours. We'll also surface p95 latency numbers per-config so you can check the SLA trade-offs.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: avery_prompt_set_v1.json (text)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + prompt sets & next steps (Avery Analytics)

Looping in a couple of internal notes from the eval ops side: 

- Quality regression risk: when we optimize for latency/cost (e.g., smaller quantized variants), we typically see a small uptick in schema parse failures. For Avery's SLA, we should baseline both model variants and enforce a stricter validation threshold (e.g., <=2% parse failures) before recommending the lower-cost model.
- Retry policy: agree with Marissa's recommendation — 2 automatic retries with augmentation, but the second retry should include a short structured example that shows the exact desired JSON keys and types. We'll also log the full token- and time-cost of retries in the report so that product can weigh cost vs. quality.
- Eval config: I'll spin up a pairwise run (redwood-stream-2-8b vs redwood-opt-1-16b-quantized) with schema checks, 2 retries, and record p95 latency per model. ETA: 48 hours after sample arrives.

--Rishi
Director, Applied ML | Redwood Inference
